scenes.section: Two ways to look at health

lines.raw: When Ram, who works at a tech startup in Kathmandu, goes to a clinic with a fever, the doctor asks: **"What is wrong with Ram, and how do I fix it?"** That is **individual care**.
lines.say: When Ram, who works at a tech startup in Kathmandu, goes to a clinic with a fever, the doctor asks: "What is wrong with Ram, and how do I fix it?" That is individual care.

lines.raw: One patient, one problem, one visit.
lines.say: One patient, one problem, one visit.

scenes.section: Two ways to look at health

lines.raw: Now imagine you are in charge of the health of **everyone** in a ward, or every employee of a company, or every member of an insurance plan.
lines.say: Now imagine you are in charge of the health of everyone in a ward, or every employee of a company, or every member of an insurance plan.

lines.raw: Your questions change: **"Who in this group is sick?
lines.say: Your questions change: "Who in this group is sick?

lines.raw: Who is about to get sick?
lines.say: Who is about to get sick?

lines.raw: Who has not been seen at all?
lines.say: Who has not been seen at all?

lines.raw: What can we do before they end up in hospital?"** That is **population health**.
lines.say: What can we do before they end up in hospital?" That is population health.

scenes.section: Two ways to look at health

lines.raw: Simple definition.
lines.say: Simple definition.

lines.raw: Population health means looking after the health of a **whole group of people**, not just the patient sitting in front of you.
lines.say: Population health means looking after the health of a whole group of people, not just the patient sitting in front of you.

lines.raw: You use data to find who needs help, reach out to them, and measure whether the whole group got healthier.
lines.say: You use data to find who needs help, reach out to them, and measure whether the whole group got healthier.

scenes.section: Two ways to look at health

lines.raw: Same health system, two points of view.
lines.say: Same health system, two points of view.

lines.raw: Who do we look at? Individual care: The patient who walked in. Population health: Everyone in the group, including people who never came in.
lines.say: Who do we look at? Individual care: The patient who walked in. Population health: Everyone in the group, including people who never came in.

lines.raw: When do we act? Individual care: When the patient feels sick. Population health: Before people get sick, or before they get worse.
lines.say: When do we act? Individual care: When the patient feels sick. Population health: Before people get sick, or before they get worse.

lines.raw: Main tool. Individual care: Examination and tests. Population health: Data: lists, counts, risk scores.
lines.say: Main tool. Individual care: Examination and tests. Population health: Data: lists, counts, risk scores.

lines.raw: Success means. Individual care: This patient got better. Population health: The whole group is healthier and care costs less per person.
lines.say: Success means. Individual care: This patient got better. Population health: The whole group is healthier and care costs less per person.

lines.raw: Typical person. Individual care: Doctor, nurse. Population health: Care manager, public health worker, data analyst.
lines.say: Typical person. Individual care: Doctor, nurse. Population health: Care manager, public health worker, data analyst.

lines.raw: Nepal already does this.
lines.say: Nepal already does this.

lines.raw: You have probably seen population health in action without calling it that.
lines.say: You have probably seen population health in action without calling it that.

lines.raw: Nepal has around **50,000 Female Community Health Volunteers (FCHVs)**, often called **"mahila swasthya swayamsevika"**.
lines.say: Nepal has around 50,000 Female Community Health Volunteers (F C H V's), often called "mahila swasthya swayamsevika".

lines.raw: Many have served their communities since the programme began in the late 1980s.
lines.say: Many have served their communities since the programme began in the late 1980s.

lines.raw: An FCHV **knows every household** in her area: who is pregnant, which children are newborn, who is old and living alone.
lines.say: An F C H V knows every household in her area: who is pregnant, which children are newborn, who is old and living alone.

lines.raw: She does not wait for people to visit a hospital.
lines.say: She does not wait for people to visit a hospital.

lines.raw: She **goes to them**: reminding mothers about check-ups, giving health advice, and pointing people to the health post.
lines.say: She goes to them: reminding mothers about check-ups, giving health advice, and pointing people to the health post.

lines.raw: During **national vaccination and vitamin A campaigns**, she helps make sure **every** eligible child in the area is reached, not only the children whose parents remembered to come.
lines.say: During national vaccination and vitamin A campaigns, she helps make sure every eligible child in the area is reached, not only the children whose parents remembered to come.

lines.raw: Health posts **count** how many children were reached, so the district can see which areas are falling behind.
lines.say: Health posts count how many children were reached, so the district can see which areas are falling behind.

lines.raw: That is population health.
lines.say: That is population health.

lines.raw: Know your whole group.
lines.say: Know your whole group.

lines.raw: Find the people who need something.
lines.say: Find the people who need something.

lines.raw: Reach out before they get sick.
lines.say: Reach out before they get sick.

lines.raw: Count the results.
lines.say: Count the results.

lines.raw: The US does exactly the same thing, but with insurance data instead of a volunteer's notebook.
lines.say: The U S does exactly the same thing, but with insurance data instead of a volunteer's notebook.

lines.raw: In Nepal: How Ram's and Sita's schemes look at the group.
lines.say: In Nepal: How Ram's and Sita's schemes look at the group.

lines.raw: With private insurance:
lines.say: With private insurance:

lines.raw: Ram's startup buys **one group policy** for all its employees.
lines.say: Ram's startup buys one group policy for all its employees.

lines.raw: When the policy is renewed, the insurer looks at the **whole group's claims** from last year, not just Ram's.
lines.say: When the policy is renewed, the insurer looks at the whole group's claims from last year, not just Ram's.

lines.raw: If many employees made big claims, the premium may go up.
lines.say: If many employees made big claims, the premium may go up.

lines.raw: So the startup has a reason to care about everyone's health, for example by arranging a yearly **health check camp** at the office.
lines.say: So the startup has a reason to care about everyone's health, for example by arranging a yearly health check camp at the office.

lines.raw: With the Social Security Fund:
lines.say: With the Social Security Fund:

lines.raw: Sita, an accountant in Kathmandu, has SSF cover that is paid for by the contributions of **many workers together**.
lines.say: Sita, an accountant in Kathmandu, has S S F cover that is paid for by the contributions of many workers together.

lines.raw: A fund like this must think about the whole group: how many contributors are getting sick, and which illnesses cost the most.
lines.say: A fund like this must think about the whole group: how many contributors are getting sick, and which illnesses cost the most.

lines.raw: Keeping the group healthy, for example through check-ups that catch problems early, helps the money last for everyone.
lines.say: Keeping the group healthy, for example through check-ups that catch problems early, helps the money last for everyone.

lines.raw: Population health in the US.
lines.say: Population health in the U S.

lines.raw: In the US: Who looks after Emily's whole group?
lines.say: In the U S: Who looks after Emily's whole group?

lines.raw: **Emily's insurer** covers thousands of members, including Emily (an office worker in Texas), her husband Daniel and their daughter Lily.
lines.say: Emily's insurer covers thousands of members, including Emily (an office worker in Texas), her husband Daniel and their daughter Lily.

lines.raw: It pays their claims, so it wants them to stay healthy.
lines.say: It pays their claims, so it wants them to stay healthy.

lines.raw: **Bluebonnet Logistics**, Emily's employer (fictional), helps pay the premium.
lines.say: Bluebonnet Logistics, Emily's employer (fictional), helps pay the premium.

lines.raw: It also wants healthy workers and lower costs.
lines.say: It also wants healthy workers and lower costs.

lines.raw: **Doctors' groups and hospitals** are more and more often paid for keeping a group of patients healthy, not just for each visit.
lines.say: Doctors' groups and hospitals are more and more often paid for keeping a group of patients healthy, not just for each visit.

lines.raw: (This is called value-based care.).
lines.say: (This is called value-based care.).

lines.raw: **Medicare**, the government plan for people aged 65 and over, covers Emily's father **Robert**.
lines.say: Medicare, the government plan for people aged 65 and over, covers Emily's father Robert.

lines.raw: Since January 2024, Robert has been on **Gulf Coast Advantage (HMO)**, a **Medicare Advantage** plan run by a different private insurer, **Gulf Coast Health Plan** (made-up names).
lines.say: Since January 2024, Robert has been on Gulf Coast Advantage (H M O), a Medicare Advantage plan run by a different private insurer, Gulf Coast Health Plan (made-up names).

lines.raw: It runs programmes for members with long-term illnesses like his diabetes.
lines.say: It runs programmes for members with long-term illnesses like his diabetes.

lines.raw: Why the money matters.
lines.say: Why the money matters.

lines.raw: In the US, a small group of very sick people uses a large share of all healthcare money.
lines.say: In the U S, a small group of very sick people uses a large share of all healthcare money.

lines.raw: If an insurer can help a person with diabetes keep their sugar under control, it may avoid a hospital stay that costs many thousands of dollars.
lines.say: If an insurer can help a person with diabetes keep their sugar under control, it may avoid a hospital stay that costs many thousands of dollars.

lines.raw: Better health and lower cost often go together.
lines.say: Better health and lower cost often go together.
